subject: Emotions
title: Awe and Time Perception
description: A micro-lesson that makes Awe and Time Perception usable.

hook.text: People watching an awe-inspiring video felt they had more time available than those watching a funny clip.

buildup.text: Researchers at Stanford found awe expands subjective time. Minutes feel longer; the rush of life slows.

discovery.text: The mechanism: awe pulls you into the present moment, reducing mental time travel to past and future.

twist.text: Feeling time-rich made people more willing to volunteer. Awe didn't just slow time—it made people generous.

climax.text: In a world obsessed with productivity, awe is the rare emotion that makes you feel less hurried.

punchline.text: Awe doesn't add minutes. It adds presence.

quiz.question: What does awe do to subjective time?
